$comment: The runtimeVersions of binaries that are actually OUT THERE — in the store, or on a
tester's phone. This file is the only thing CI can consult to answer 'would anyone
receive this update?', and getting that wrong is invisible: a publish aimed at a
runtimeVersion nobody has succeeds, reports success, and reaches no one.
KEYED BY CHANNEL, because a channel is not a label on one binary. `RELEASE_CHANNEL` is
read by app.config.js (it becomes the `expo-channel-name` request header), and the
fingerprint hashes the RESOLVED config — so the same commit built for staging and for
production has two different runtimeVersions. A staging tester and a store user are
running different binaries, and each channel can only be published to if ITS binary
exists. A single flat list would have made every staging publish skip.
That is a feature worth keeping: the channel header and the runtimeVersion separate
the two audiences independently, so a staging bundle cannot reach a production phone
even if a channel mapping were wrong.
ADD AN ENTRY when you upload a build to the store or hand an APK to testers. REMOVE
one when no device can still be running it — an entry left behind only means CI is
willing to publish for a runtimeVersion nobody has, which is harmless but pointless.
Get the value from the build itself, never by re-resolving it later from a tree that
has moved on:
eas build:list --platform android --json --non-interactive | jq '.[0].runtimeVersion'
or, from a local --local build's artifact:
unzip -p <app>.aab base/assets/fingerprint     # app bundle
unzip -p <app>.apk assets/fingerprint          # apk

production.note: first Play upload — app bundle, built locally with eas build --local

staging.note: first staging APK — build-artifacts/lmthing-staging.apk, eas build --profile staging --local. versionCode 8 is shared with the production vc8 AAB (appVersionSource is remote and the staging profile does not autoIncrement); the two are still different binaries on different runtimeVersions, so the number identifies nothing on its own here.
